name: Deep Ocean, Vast Sea
objectiveText: Recover the Silver Dawning's Lockbox and the Mist Veil's Lockbox for Gorbold Steelhand in Auberdine. Both items should be found aboard the wreckage of the ships to the north of the village. Silver Dawning's Lockbox  ( 1 ) Mist Veil's Lockbox  ( 1 )

comments.body: Beware of murlocs swimming through walls. It can happen with alarming frequency.

Just FYI, each box is located in the bottom of the boat in the stern (back) end of the ship. Both ships sank with their prow (front) end pointing towards land, so the stern is the seaward side of each ship. 

There is also a "weapons crate" in the very center of the bottom hold of the south ship. Hard to get to, because there are many close spawns and a hole in the hull nearby where you can get adds coming in from outside the ship.
These are around 39,28 in Darkshore

The two ships can be found at 39, 28. You have to pick up Mist Veil's Lockbox from the ship lying on its side before Silver Dawning's Lockbox will spawn in the other ship.

Both lockboxes can be opened from the outside of the ship. Just stand behind the ship and move your cursor around until you find the box.

comments.body: Both boxes are heavily guarded by wicked fast little sea monkeys that are almost impossible to pull without one or more adds.

Unless you're a warlock, have an underwater breathing potion or two, are too high-level for it to be meaningful, are a marine mammal in another life or are a closet masochist, this is one you can skip. The rewards are not very good, the XP isn't worth it to offset the time spent, the Darn rep is OK but you'll wonder afterwards how you're ever going to get that lost time back. I love Classic and loved it the first time around but as many others have said, I can confirm that this is not one of its memorable quests.

Did this solo as a 17 hunter. Only death was my pet, once.

First of all, not sure if this matters or not, but I did the north ship first (Mist's Veil). Went around to the side with the big hole in it, stayed just under the surface where the camera shows underwater, but you don't start holding your breath. Targeted a murloc, sent the pet in, and hit follow button to pull it back when he got their attention. When the murloc was almost in range, sent the pet back in, and proceeded to light the little bugger up. Wash, rinse, repeat. Lost the pet when it pulled 4 out, but killed two of the murlocs and swam for my life. The clams are a frequent drop, so if your pet eats clam meat like mine does, no worries about happiness loss.

Got all the fish outside out of the way, then waited for the ones inside to show up through the hole, target, and sent pet, etc. Swam down a couple times to check if the way was clear, eventually it was, and went inside to grab the lockbox. Oh, forgot to mention, used Eagle Eye from a safe distance to make sure I knew where the thing was, a major help.

First lockbox down, headed south, keeping clear of the murlocs. Used Eagle Eye again, eventually spotted the lockbox for the Silver Dawning. In the process, noticed the following:

A. The lockbox was easily accesible from a gunport-looking entrance in the side of the ship, near the back.

B. There were almost NO murlocs nearby outside, and from what I could see, absolutely none inside near the gunport and box.

Intruiged, I killed all of 2 murlocs outside, put my pet on stay, and headed in. 10 seconds in, 5 seconds to loot, and 10-15 seconds out. No muss, only fuss was when I lost the exit hole for a moment. Method might even work on the first ship, don't know. Damn near necessary on the Dawning, the thing is crawling with murlocs.

So, moral of the long-winded story: doing your planning carefully can save you an IMMENSE amount of trouble. Hope this is helpful.

Rogues may be able to SOLO this, but if you arent a rogue, you can do this with just two people. THe nearest graveyard is so CLOSE, it isnt even a hassel dying. 

The trick?

Both you and your partner go balls to the wall, and swim inside each vessel, and get as close as you can to the chest you seek before you most ultimately die. 

When you and your partner return as  ghosts, wisp back to the location of the chest in each ship, and have your partner ressurect first. While your partner creates a diversion, and starts to get slaughtered...ressurect yourself, open the chest, get the loot. Then swim your ass off as fast as you can outside the ship. Hopefully before you, TOO, are slaughtered, you can get far away from the monster weasels, and then you and your partner can trade places. 

Works everytime, Trust me.

I managed to complete this quest legit as a lvl 20 hunter last night.

First I would take out as many swimming around the part of the ship with the chests as I could.  Next came the tricky part.  I would swim close enough to the ship and hit my button to target the closest enemy.  Even though you can't see them, you can still target them inside the ship.  Then I would lay a trap down and tell my pet to attack the target.  Sure enough he would swim into the ship and I would wait for him to get attacked.  As soon as he did, I would switch my pet to passive so that he would break off the attack and start swimming back to me with at least 1 or 2 nasties hot on his tail.  As soon as I could see a target, I'd start hitting them with my arrows and when they got to me the trap would do a lot of damage and I would tell my pet to attack again and we'd kill them.  About every 3rd time or so of doing that I'd get about 4 or 5 on us and I'd die because it would take too long and my breath would run out or they're would just be too many of them.  Even if I swam to the surface and caught my breath, they would still usually kill me because there be 2 or 3 and once they killed my pet, I was easy prey.  So after about 3 deaths like this I finally had pretty much cleared the ship of all the baddies and swam in and looted and swam out unharmed.  Then I did it again on the other ship.

I've completed the quest using a lvl 15 hunter. It took me at least 6 or 7 lives to do it, here's why.

At the same time as I was doing the quest there was also like 3 other people doing it. 

I lost three lives on the first chest in this way:
Life 1: Opening chest... bar is almost filled.... all of a sudden one of the people starts swimming from around the corner closely followed by about 2 thrashers and three of the little creatures. You would think that they would continue and follow that player? No. As soon as they saw me all of em turned on me.

Life2: Swimming towards the chest, same player as before starts swimming towards me, dragging 2 thrashers and 2 creatures. Dead again...

Life3: Getting very suspicious now. I've inspected the area, and it looks clear. I get to the bottom almost to the chest and two other players swim by me... you know what follows. This time though I sent my cat to distract the creatures. It worked well(he has roar), for about 10 seconds, and as Im getting away I get ambushed by 1 creature and the rest catch up....

Second chest

Unless you are gonna attack this quest in a group, dont waste your time.

Why should you not waste your time:

#1-the item reward are common gloves and if you are a leather wearer, you cant even use it.

#2-you do get 18s, but I spend over 2/3s of that amount repairing my equipment during and after this quest.

#3-you do get IF rep, which is nice if you are a NE, but you can gain IF rep much easier then this.

#4-it is not part of a chain

All-in-all, the risks far out way the rewards here.   Plus, if you are not a druid with aquatic form or have some means to breathe underwater, the quest is only more a pain in the ass.

comments.body:
I strongly recommend you have an aquatic form for this quest. If you do not have an aquatic form, then at least group up.  I attempted this with groups several times, without success.  I eventually did it solo, but only with aquatic form.

Regardless of which lockbox you attempt first, you will have to enter the ship to open it.  I couldn't open the lockboxes from the outside.

1st Lockbox - Ship closest to Auberdine.  Enter through a hole in the north side of the ship.  The lockbox will be to your right on the same level.

2nd Lockbox - Ship on it's side.  Enter from the top level and fight your way down.  Murlocs are everywhere, and you will have to kill all of them as you.  This is not an easy swim, even with aquatic form.  You will have to go to the very bottom of the ship to find the lockbox.  By the time you make your way to the bottom, the Murlocs will most likely be back.
For me, the boxes were near the aft (rear) of the ships. Come in about center of the back side of the ship. You should be able to locate the boxes from outside.
replies: I can confirm the boxes were both in 'openable' objects in the aft (rear) of the hold (lowest level) of the ships, which is great because the main deck is a nightmare to maneuver around in with limited breath.

comments.body: The Lockboxes can no longer be looted from the outside (through the stern) of the ships.
replies: This is still working via the "Interact with Target" keybind in Options from outside both ships.
